newsitem.title: USA: U.S., South and North Korea discuss peace talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., South and North Korea discuss peace talks.

text.p: U.S., North and South Korean officials met in New York Friday in a fresh bid to arrange four-party talks on a peace settlement for the Korean peninsula, the State Department said.

The low-level meeting was the first between the three countries since more senior officials met in New York April 16-21 in an inconclusive effort to thrash out details of the talks proposed last year by the United States and South Korea.
Washington and Seoul are trying to lure North Korea into negotiations, also involving China, that would seek a permanent settlement to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.

Pyongyang agreed in principle in April to take part in such negotiations, but diplomats said it was seeking major food aid first to alleviate famine in North Korea. Washington says such aid can only come once the talks are under way.
State Department spokesman John Dinger played down prospects of any major breakthrough Friday.
"These diplomatic contacts are moving in the right direction, but we do not expect to have something new to report after each meeting," he told reporters. "This is a process, a steady process."

Friday's talks were attended for the United States by Mark Minton, director of the State Department's office of Korean affairs, and National Security Council Asia director Jack Pritchard; for South Korea by Washington embassy counsellor Soo Hyuck Lee; and for North Korea by Li Gun, deputy permanent representative to the United Nations.
